To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the surface oxidation of Cd, Sn, Sb and In is studied using X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy.
the surface oxidation of cadmium and indium is much faster than that of tin and antimony.
the oxidation of In and Cd is more pronounced than that of Sn and Sb.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the oxidation of metals and semiconductors by X ray photoelectron spectroscopy.
the surface chemistry of metals.
the development of a new class of compounds with potential applications in the fields of catalysis, electrochemistry, and electronics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
surface oxidation of the elements studied proceeds by the formation of a surface oxide layer of a composition which depends on the metal, the surface preparation and the ambient atmosphere.
the photoelectron and Aug er techniques have proved to be very useful and informative tools for the investigation of surface oxidation.

the surface oxidation of In, Sn and Cd proceeds by an oxygen chemisorption mechanism and the formation of the surface oxides is due to a subsequent reaction of chemisorbed oxygen with the metal surface.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the surface oxidation is not a single process.
the photoelectron spectroscopy is a very useful tool in surface science.
the surface oxides are formed by the reaction of oxygen molecules with metal atoms on the surface.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the oxidation of the metal surfaces is not a trivial process.
it is possible to use the XPS and AES spectra to identify the surface oxidation states of the metals.

the surface oxidation of Cd, Sn and In proceeds in a manner similar to the surface oxidation of Al, Ga and In, and the surface oxides of these elements are also similar to the surface oxides formed on Al, Ga and Zn.
